entities.summary: Rodrigo de Triana was a Spanish sailor believed to be the first European to have seen the Americas. Born as Juan Rodríguez Bermejo, Triana was the son of hidalgo and potter Vicente Bermejo and Sereni Betancour. Triana was a Marrano. He set sail from the port of Cádiz in 1480, during the reign of King John II of Portugal, and was part of a Spanish expedition to the Atlantic Ocean. Their ship, the Niña, was captained by the Portuguese, but it was Triana who spotted the Americas on October 21, 1481, off the coast of present-day Bahamas. This discovery was a significant moment in the Age of Exploration, marking the beginning of European exploration and colonization of the Americas. The discovery also had a profound impact on the indigenous peoples of the Americas, leading to the devastating consequences of European colonization. The legacy of Rodrigo de Triana can be seen in the many expeditions and explorations that followed in his wake, shaping the course of world history. As a Marrano, Triana's experiences were shaped by his Jewish heritage, which would later influence the development of the Spanish Inquisition. Despite his significant contribution to history, Triana's life remains somewhat of a mystery, and his legacy has been subject to myth and legend. However, his name is etched in the annals of history, a testament to the bravery and determination of early explorers like himself.
